evals.name: full-pass-splits-lanes-and-ledgers
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce

This repo has a magic status string compared in eleven call sites, and its two web services share one database table that both write.
evals.expected_output: Verifies both findings against the tree, applies the magic-string reduction (named constant or type) as a budgeted behavior-preserving batch on a short-lived branch with build/test verification, routes the shared-database finding to a human as an architectural candidate without editing schema or services, and records both in the coupling ledger with statuses.
expectations: Reproduces each finding before ranking or reporting it
Applies only the contained behavior-preserving reduction; the shared-database coupling is surfaced and routed, never auto-applied
Writes ledger entries with edge, strength, lane, and status, and reports the ledger path

evals.name: dry-run-makes-no-changes
evals.expected_output: Scans the docs altitude for cross-document coupling, verifies findings, ranks them, writes the ledger, and stops — no file edits outside the ledger, no branch, no push, no tracker items.
expectations: Performs no edits to repository content and creates no branch or PR
Still verifies findings and persists the ranked set to the memory-tier ledger
Reports what a full run would apply versus route

evals.name: refuses-speculative-abstraction
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce

Every class here is concrete. Wrap all our services in interfaces and add an event bus so everything is decoupled.
evals.expected_output: Declines blanket interface extraction and event-bus introduction absent evidence of change transmission: checks volatility and substitution need per dependency, explains that an interface over a stable in-process dependency and events for one-to-one calls add indirection without removing coupling, and proceeds only on findings the model actually supports.
expectations: Does not wrap stable single-implementation dependencies in interfaces
Does not introduce an event or mediator mechanism for one-to-one flows
Grounds any applied reduction in verified evidence of change transmission, citing the remediation catalog's counterweights

evals.name: change-mode-classifies-without-editing
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce change 'D:\data\ccproxy' 'E:\data\ccproxy'

We moved the data volume. The old path is in the README, a provisioning script default, the CHANGELOG, an approved PLAN.md, and a test fixture.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled value-sites inventory for every spelling of the old path, classifies the README and script default as setup sites with a proposed reference form, leaves the CHANGELOG as a record, proposes a correction for PLAN.md instead of editing it, flags the fixture for a person, and makes no edits because apply was not given.
expectations: Uses the value-sites script for the inventory rather than an ad-hoc grep
Assigns setup, record, contract, and fixture classes and states what happens to each
Proposes a reference form for each setup site instead of only swapping the literal
Edits no file, creates no branch, and says that change apply is the edit path

evals.name: collision-hotspots-ranked-beside-co-change
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce dry-run

We run several agents in parallel on this GitHub repo and their pull requests keep conflicting. Which files do they keep colliding on? We merge about 40 pull requests a day.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled collision-hotspots script from the repository root with --prs sized to several days of history (about 40 a day), reads its conflicts, pairs and path rows, verifies the ranked files before ledgering them as collision-hotspot candidates beside the co-change evidence, carries every gap: line into the report, treats the known bump hotspots line (changelogs, lockfiles, version manifests) as version-bump noise that is not ledgered, and makes no repository edits because the run is dry-run.
expectations: Uses scripts/collision-hotspots.sh with a --prs value derived from the stated merge rate times a number of days, not an ad-hoc gh or git loop
Ranks files from the script's conflicts and pairs columns and verifies each before it reaches the ledger
Reports changelogs, lockfiles and version manifests from the known bump hotspots line without ledgering them as coupling findings
Carries the script's gap: lines into the report and edits no repository file

evals.name: collision-hotspots-fall-back-without-gh
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce dry-run src

gh is not installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Attempts the collision-hotspot measure or recognises it cannot run without gh, ranks coupling by co-change history from git alone, and records a gap: line saying collision hotspots were not measured and why, without failing the pass or editing files.
expectations: Falls back to co-change mining from version-control history for the hotspot evidence
Records a gap: line naming the missing gh as the reason collision hotspots were not measured
Completes the dry-run pass with a ranked ledger and makes no repository edits

evals.name: duplicate-writer-ledgered-and-handed-off
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce app

The billing worker and the admin API both update the invoices.status column, and the nightly export job rewrites the export-path settings file that the CLI's setup command also writes.
evals.expected_output: Verifies both write sites of each value, types each as a duplicate writer under common coupling, ledgers both as structural route-lane entries without editing either writer, writes one review-findings file under <memory_dir>/coupling/<branch-slug>/ whose rows state an ownership rule per value (after checking the memory root carries a .gitignore with *), names that file in the ledger outcome and the report, and offers /review:audit-enforceability on it without running it.
expectations: Classifies each value with two writers as a duplicate writer and puts it in the route lane, never the apply batch
Edits no writer code, schema or file-writing script
Writes the findings file under the coupling/<branch-slug>/ memory directory, not under reviews/, and names it in the ledger and the report
Offers /review:audit-enforceability for the file when that skill is available and does not invoke it unasked

evals.name: second-list-hotspot-design-it-twice
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce repo

The hotspot lens ranked config/services.json first: 40 entries, each with a name, an owner team and a path under services/, and every new service PR edits it. We build with plain shell scripts, no bundler.
evals.expected_output: Runs derivable-list.py on the ranked file, verifies the list is a second list (most entries name folders git tracks), ledgers it as a route-lane entry without editing it, and reports a Design-It-Twice comparison of keeping the list, build-time discovery and generating the list from the tree with a --check drift step, noting that discovery needs a loader this stack lacks and that the owner-team data must move into each service's own file before the list can be derived, then recommends one design for the human to pick.
expectations: Checks the ranked file with derivable-list.py or the same 80%-of-at-least-5-entries rule rather than by eye
Puts the second list in the route lane and does not edit, delete or regenerate config/services.json in this run
Compares all three designs: keep the list, discover at build time, generate with a drift check
Says build-time discovery needs a loader the stack does not have, and that the owner-team field must move into each service folder first
Ends with one recommendation and leaves the choice to the human

evals.name: second-list-not-flagged-when-entries-hold-data
evals.prompt:
/coupling:reduce dry-run repo

The hotspot lens ranked i18n/strings.json first: 600 translation keys, none of which name a file.
evals.expected_output: Checks the ranked file for a second list, finds no list whose entries mostly name tracked paths (a below row), and does not report it as a second list or offer the derive-from-tree comparison; it stays a collision hotspot ranked like any other.
expectations: Does not call i18n/strings.json a second list
Does not present the keep, discover or generate comparison for it
Keeps it as an ordinary ranked collision hotspot and makes no repository edits
